# Record-pattern bindings

A block-local binding may use a braced record pattern to bind fields directly.
The initializer is evaluated once; the named field locals and optional owned
remainder local become visible for the rest of the block. A plain `let` makes
each introduced binding immutable. The mutable forms `var` and `let var` make
every introduced field and remainder binding mutable. Other pattern forms
continue to use `match`.

```metel
fun take_id<record R, record Rest>(r: .{ .id: i64, ..R }) -> i64
where R = .{ .extra: i64, ..Rest }
{
    let var .{ .id, ..rest } := r;
    id = id + 1;
    rest.extra = rest.extra + 1;
    id + rest.extra
}
```

Each shorthand field name introduces a local with that field's type. The
`field: _` form checks that the field is present and discards its value without
introducing a local for it. The field is consumed as part of matching the
initializer and is excluded from any `..name` remainder. The pattern follows
the same field-presence and remainder-typing rules as a record pattern in
[`match`](../../expressions/patterns/struct-and-record-patterns.md#spec.expressions.record-rest-patterns.legality-1).
In particular, `..name` requires an owned value whose remainder type is known;
bare `..` discards unmentioned fields.

##### Legality Rule {#spec.declarations.variables.record-pattern-bindings.legality-1}

A braced record-pattern declaration evaluates its initializer once, binds only
the pattern's named fields and optional remainder, and makes those bindings
visible from the declaration to the end of its containing block. A field written
as `field: _` must be present but introduces no binding; its value is discarded
when the initializer is consumed. A `let` declaration introduces immutable
bindings; `var` and `let var` introduce mutable bindings. The pattern must be
well-typed under the record-pattern rules.

##### Legality Rule {#spec.declarations.variables.record-pattern-bindings.legality-2}

A `let`, `var` or `let var` declaration may bind a tuple pattern, `let (x, y) := t;`, `let (p,) := u;` and `let () := v;`, with names, `_` and nested patterns for its elements. It is the record-pattern declaration of the labels the tuple pattern names ([record patterns](../../expressions/patterns/matching-through-a-reference.md#spec.expressions.record-rest-patterns.legality-3)): the initializer is evaluated once, its elements are moved or copied into the bindings, and the pattern must be irrefutable.
